title: Mini sprint metrics cheat-sheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick compact reference I carry during 1-week prompt/model sprints. One page I can paste into a PR or short retro. Not polished — notes to self.

Top-level rules of thumb:
- Target median p95 latency < 180ms for interactive features.
- If avg tokens per call > 250, consider minibatching or KV prefix cache.
- Cost estimate per call = (tokens_out + tokens_in) * model_unit_cost (approx)

Mini table (append latest rows during run)
| date | prompt-id | model | quant | batch | latency(ms) | tokens | est-cost($) | qual(1-5) | notes |
| 2026-02-01 | P-024 | rw-xxl-v1 | int8 | 1 | 142 | 180 | 0.008 | 4 | good coherence, slight repeat |
| 2026-02-04 | P-028 | rw-xxl-v1 | fp16 | 2 | 210 | 420 | 0.017 | 4 | batching raises p95, but cost down |
| 2026-02-10 | P-031 | open-xl-8k | q4_0 | 1 | 175 | 95 | 0.003 | 3 | cheaper but hallucination on dates |

Quick calculations (cheats):
- sample cost calc: tokens 200 * $0.00001/token = $0.002 per call
- effective per-user cost (50 calls/day) = 50 * per-call cost = $0.10/day

Observations to capture during sprint:
- latency swings correlate w/ batch size and system load — tag test rows with region and time if p95 spikes.
- quality drift: create a micro prompt-set (10 examples) and record qual(1-5) after any model tweak.

Short checklist before changes:
[ ] Add 10 canonical prompts to micro-eval set
[ ] Run sweep: quantization presets (fp16,int8,q4_0)
[ ] Measure 500 calls per config (aggregated across 5 mins)
[ ] Snapshot token distributions and p95

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add automated script that writes this table back to a tiny CSV in repo (scripts/mini_sprint_snapshot.sh).
- Check Redwood Optimize recommendations for quant-profile that fits P-0xx workloads.
- Follow up with SRE if p95 > 300ms consistently for any config.

Context links:
- GH PR with experiment harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-experiments/pull/312
- Linear ticket for production checklist: LINEAR-4551

End of sheet — keep it intentionally short and copyable.
